## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

<sub>[context source](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct/blob/48d87cd5e0523b430d77e93becd3655cd6897230/README.md): Context length stated on the official model card.</sub>

<pre>
download                      size  score
4-bit q4_k_m                ~8.9GB   44.9
8-bit q8_0                 ~17.3GB   44.9
4-bit Q4_K_M                ~8.6GB   44.9
8-bit Q8_0                 ~14.8GB   44.9

<sub>The score is the published model's; quantized downloads haven't been evaluated separately.</sub>

### Run it on your own machine

**llama.cpp** · install: macOS / Linux `curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh` · Windows `irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex` · [other ways](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md) · Homebrew and winget installs name the commands llama-cli and llama-server instead.

```sh
# 4-bit Q4_K_M · ~8.6GB
llama cli -hf bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
llama serve -hf bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# 8-bit Q8_0 · ~14.8GB
llama cli -hf bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF:Q8_0
# or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
llama serve -hf bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF:Q8_0
```

**LM Studio** · install: [macOS / Windows / Linux](https://lmstudio.ai/download) · Open the app once before using the lms command.

```sh
# 4-bit Q4_K_M · ~8.6GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF@Q4_K_M -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
# 8-bit Q8_0 · ~14.8GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF@Q8_0 -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
# 4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only · ~7.9GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-4bit -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
# 4-bit mlx-8bit · mac only · ~14.8GB
lms get https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-8bit -y
# then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name
```

**Ollama** · install: [macOS / Windows](https://ollama.com/download) · Linux `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`

```sh
# 4-bit q4_k_m · ~8.9GB
ollama run phi3:14b-medium-4k-instruct-q4_K_M
# 8-bit q8_0 · ~17.3GB
ollama run phi3:14b-medium-4k-instruct-q8_0
# 4-bit Q4_K_M · ~8.6GB
ollama run hf.co/bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M
# 8-bit Q8_0 · ~14.8GB
ollama run hf.co/bartowski/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-GGUF:Q8_0
```

**MLX (Mac)** · install: with uv `uv tool install mlx-lm` · or `pip install mlx-lm` · Apple silicon Macs only, text only.

```sh
# 4-bit mlx-4bit · mac only · ~7.9GB
mlx_lm.chat --model mlx-community/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-4bit
# or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-4bit
# 4-bit mlx-8bit · mac only · ~14.8GB
mlx_lm.chat --model mlx-community/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-8bit
# or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct-8bit
```
